”Reclining chair no 36”
Bruno Mathsson (1907 - 1988)

Artist/Maker
Designer: Bruno Mathsson (1907 - 1988)
Made by: Firma Karl Mathsson

Dates
Designed: Designed 1936
Manufactured: Manufactured 1939

Bentlaminated birch, plywood, plaited webbing

h x l: Mått 82 x 140 cm

Purchase 2010 Carl Adolf Weber Fund

Other titles
Title (sv): "Liggstol nr 36"
Title (en): ”Reclining chair no 36”
Label (sv): Liggstol nr 36
Label (en): Reclining chair no 36

Description
Description: Mathsson learned cabinet-making from his father and studied on his own. Inspired by the ideas of functionalism, he explored the “mechanics of sitting” by seating himself in snow, measuring the imprints made by his body, and converting the measurements into durable furniture in creative shapes with built-in springiness made of laminated wood. This resource-efficient technique consists of gluing layers of wood veneer together and inserting them into a pressing tool.

Exhibited
Nationalmuseum -> Room 1412 1920-1965

Collection
Furniture (Applied art and design)

Geographical origin
Geographical origin: Värnamo (Sweden, Jönköping County)

Material
Weave (Textiles), Birch (Wood)

Object category
Chair (Furniture)

Additional texte
Description: Bruno Mathsson said that ’furniture should be designed with such skill that sitting in them requires none at all.’ For several decades, he came to symbolise Swedish design abroad. The first chair he designed was Gräshoppan, in 1931, and in the 1980s he made furniture for computers. Liggstol nr 36 is among his most sculptural designs, with a curvature that almost seems to hover.
